findings.issue: Error message interpolates `res.status`/`res.statusText` but the fetch callback parameter is `response`; any non-OK API response throws a ReferenceError instead of the intended error. It is only masked because every caller catches all errors and treats them as 'not found', which also misclassifies server errors as 404s.
findings.suggestion: Use `response.status`/`response.statusText` (or throw the existing ApiError class), and add a unit test that a 404 rejects with the status in the message.

findings.issue: No test script, runner, or single test file despite ~780 lines of script logic, most of it pure data transformation that is trivially unit-testable (format.ts, buildMoveTables, evolutionTree, pagination).
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (already using vite) with unit tests for format.ts, data.ts's pure functions, and the api.ts error/cache paths; add a `test` script.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache stores the promise, so a rejected fetch is cached forever: one transient API hiccup permanently poisons that endpoint for the process lifetime, and callers that don't catch (e.g. getPokemonCard via api) will 500 on every subsequent render.
findings.suggestion: Delete the cache entry when the promise rejects, and add a test for the failure-then-retry path.

findings.issue: Type filter re-implements URL-id parsing with an inline regex (`/\/(\d+)\/?$/`) instead of reusing idFromUrl/isSpeciesId from app/src/lib/api.ts:37-43; the two implementations differ subtly (query-string handling) and will drift.
findings.suggestion: Reuse idFromUrl/isSpeciesId and cover both with one test.

findings.issue: buildMoveTables encodes many spec rules (fixed method order Level Up/Machine/Egg/Tutor then alphabetical, level-up sorted by level then name, others by name) with no tests; a future tweak to sorting will only be caught by the external e2e suite, if at all.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test buildMoveTables with a small fixture covering method order, level-up ordering, and unexpected methods.

findings.issue: Client-side sorting relies on empty-string data-sort-value to detect missing values, manual numeric parsing, and aria-sort attribute toggling; none is tested, and regressions here (e.g. '10' < '9' string sort) would surface only in full e2e runs.
findings.suggestion: Add Playwright component/DOM tests (or extract the comparator into a pure function and unit-test missing-last, numeric vs text, and direction flip).

findings.issue: Hidden-ability aggregation ORs is_hidden across duplicate pokemon entries via a Map; this subtle logic is untested, and a refactor could silently flip 'Hidden ability' markers.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with a fixture where the same pokemon appears twice, once hidden and once not.

findings.issue: Fallback `Number(detail?.order ?? idFromUrl(ref.url) ?? 0)` yields NaN when the version-group detail fetch fails, making version-group sort order unstable (NaN comparisons).
findings.suggestion: Coalesce to a finite number and test the null-detail path.

findings.issue: Pagination clamping (page beyond last, page=abc → NaN, empty ?page= → 0, zero-match totalPages) is untested edge logic.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the clamp expression or extract it into a pure helper with tests.

findings.issue: ApiError is defined but never thrown — dead code indicating the error path was written and never wired up or exercised.
findings.suggestion: Throw ApiError in api() and assert on it in a unit test, or delete the class.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no runner, no script, not a single assertion — and relies entirely on the external acceptance suite. That has already let a real bug ship: a ReferenceError in api.ts's error path (res vs response) that is silently masked by blanket catches. The codebase is unusually rich in pure, easily testable transform logic (formatting, move-table ordering, pagination, filtering), so adding a small vitest suite plus a few DOM tests for client sorting would be low-cost and high-value.
